property_summary: Call transfer with a token that returns true from transferFrom: reference passes require(_s) and returns true, mutant rejects require(!_s) and reverts.

Call transfer with a token that returns false from transferFrom: the reference reverts because require(_s) fails, while the mutant does not revert because require(!_s) passes, causing a revert difference.

When transfer is called with _tos containing two distinct recipients, the reference contract transfers tokens to both (i=0 and i=1), while the buggy contract skips the first recipient (i=1) and only transfers to the second, resulting in a different number of successful transfers.

When the 'tos' array has length 3, the reference transfers to all three addresses via transferFrom, but the mutant with i+=2 transfers only to indices 0 and 2 (skipping index 1), so after the call, the token balance of the address at index 1 remains unchanged (e.g., 0) in the mutant whereas it would have increased (e.g., to v) in the reference.

When _tos has length 3, reference transfers v tokens to all three addresses via transferFrom, while mutant skips index 1, so address _tos[1] token balance is 0 after mutant call but v after reference call.
